Neither shows on the photo, which reads as the sharper, more authoritative source. (Carries checkpoint CP1, plaque half.)

Printed small, the ink GAINED: the keystone device's two fine parallel interior rules have run together into a single thick bar and the ribbon banner's counters have filled solid, a closure invisible on the sheet and obvious only beside the plaque trace at suite-plate size. The crest occupies only a small part of a large scan, so a high-resolution-looking file is really a small source in a big file and nothing downstream may enlarge it. (Carries checkpoint CP1, letterhead half.)

In the shaded stone reveal the pale limestone surround and the tarnished brass plaque field run to almost the same value ALONG THE LEFT EDGE, so an automatic isolation of the plaque area reports success, previews convincingly at check scale and bites that edge, leaving a crescent of the old engraving inside the supposedly cleared field and a ragged stone boundary that only shows at full resolution. (Carries checkpoint CP3.)
